title: Visiting Bunk for lessons and the Calypso melody
summary: Blumberg went to Bunk's afternoons to find his secrets, and Bunk played a Calypso tune he had picked up in Harlem.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah, I remember the concert, and I remember being kind of disappointed, and you know, the funk just felt so bad, and so forth. But anyway, those were the lessons. I mean, he invited me up to spend the afternoons with him and take lessons or what have you, you know. And I'd come up to wherever he was, and usually he was in. Every now and then he'd be out someplace. I'd have to scout around the neighborhood and look in the corner drugstore or the neighborhood bar, wherever, try to figure out where he went off to, you know. And, but sometimes we'd just sit there and talk all afternoon, wouldn't even get to play horn at all. Because actually I wasn't as interested in taking actual lessons as I was in trying to figure out what his secrets were. I mean, I heard a magic in his playing that had me all agog, you know. And I was just trying to plumb the secrets of it somehow. I was trying to figure out, had he listened a lot to Calypso music or what. I mean, there was something, some quality in his playing, a rhythmic quality that I just couldn't put my finger on. But it, it was.
Well, you mentioned the other day about that Calypso that he once went up. What was that?

Yeah, well, there was one time when, when, I guess it was one of those afternoons, I went up there and he said, well, last night I played in a little session, this was up in Harlem, in a bar down the street. And there were a bunch of West Indians there, he said, and I played, we played this tune. And he took out his horn and played some beautiful little Calypso melody that I'd never heard before or since. And I wrote it down. It was so nice, but I, I lost the paper it was written on. But I remember how striking it was. He played Calypso, I mean, that particular piece, like a, like a native Calypso player. He really had that, that feeling very, very strongly. And, and it was something that I just, uh, was trying to figure out just where his, uh, where his feet were, you know, and what, what style of music and trying to figure out how to, how to think about the man.
